headline: DARE/ICAR Committed Towards Swachhata and Reducing Pendency During Special Campaign 6.0
fullText:

DARE/ICAR Committed Towards Swachhata and Reducing Pendency During Special Campaign 6.0

16 SEP 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) will undertake Special Campaign 6.0, being observed by the Government of India from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, with a focus on Swachhata and reducing pendency in Government offices.

During the previous Special Campaign 5.0, DARE/ICAR undertook sustained efforts towards the disposal of pending references on a monthly basis and strengthened its focus on timely redressal of public grievances. During the campaign, the Ministry disposed of the maximum number of Public Grievances and Public Grievance Appeals, reflecting its continued efforts towards reducing pendency and improving grievance redressal.

As part of Special Campaign 5.0, awareness about the campaign was created across branches of DARE/ICAR throughout the country. Various activities were undertaken with emphasis on health, food safety, waste-to-wealth initiatives, hygiene and sanitation, tree plantation, enhancement of office premises, environment-friendly practices, beautification, space management and conservation measures.

DARE/ICAR also continued its efforts towards paperless functioning through the e-File system. During the campaign, targets relating to the disposal of physical files and review and closure of e-Files were achieved as part of record-management practices. These efforts resulted in the freeing up of office space and disposal of accumulated scrap and waste.

Building on the experience and outcomes of Special Campaign 5.0, DARE/ICAR is committed to further strengthening its efforts during Special Campaign 6.0, with continued emphasis on cleanliness, efficient record management, reduction of pendency, paperless functioning and better utilisation of office spaces.

(Release ID: 2310868)

headline: Department of Health & Family Welfare to launch Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October 2026 to promote Swachhata and minimize pendency in Government offices
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Department of Health & Family Welfare to launch Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October 2026 to promote Swachhata and minimize pendency in Government offices

Preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6 underway from 15th to 30th September 2026, leading to the October drive focused on effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, workspace cleanliness and efficiency

From November 2025 to August 2026, over 65,000 files reviewed, 47,000 plus grievances disposed, and 659 cleanliness campaigns conducted by DoHFW continuing the activities of Special Campaign

16 SEP 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Government’s continued focus on institutionalising Swachhata and improving efficiency in Government functioning, the Department of Health & Family Welfare (DoHFW), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, has been undertaking comprehensive cleanliness, record management and pendency reduction initiatives across its offices and institutions since 2021.

As part of these efforts, significant progress has been made in cleanliness, record management, grievance redressal and space management. During the period from November 2025 to August 2026, DoHFW reviewed 65,329 files, of which 27,531 files were weeded out. The exercise has contributed towards streamlining record management and reducing accumulated records in government offices and institutions.

During the same period, 47,537 public grievances and 3,635 associated appeals were disposed of. In addition, 543 Members of Parliament (MP) References, 19 Parliamentary Assurances and 46 State Government References were also disposed of.

As part of the cleanliness and space management initiatives, a total of 659 cleanliness campaigns were conducted across various offices and institutions. These campaigns resulted in the disposal of scrap material worth ₹21.26 lakh and the freeing up of 24,299 square feet of space. The initiatives have contributed to creating cleaner and healthier workplace environments, improved record management and more effective utilisation of available space, besides facilitating revenue generation through the disposal of scrap.

National Institute of Tuberculosis and Respiratory Diseases (NITRD), New Delhi

The Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 commenced on September 15, 2026 and will continue till September 30, 2026. During this phase, DoHFW will identify pendency under the identified parameters, mobilise ground-level functionaries, finalise sites for cleanliness campaigns, review records, undertake space management planning and identify scrap material for disposal.

Paper Waste Recycling Initiative (WWWF) at NITRD, New Delhi

The Department will make sustained efforts during the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 to achieve the objectives of the campaign and further institutionalise cleanliness, efficiency and effective record and space management across its offices and institutions.

AIIMS, Rajkot (Waste to Art)

DoHFW remains committed to creating cleaner, more efficient and better-managed Government workspaces.

(Release ID: 2310866)

headline: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Reinforces Swachhata and Digital Governance through Sustained Campaign Initiatives
fullText:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs

Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Reinforces Swachhata and Digital Governance through Sustained Campaign Initiatives

16 SEP 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs undertook a comprehensive range of activities under Special Campaign 5.0, with emphasis on cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of pending matters, space optimisation and promotion of paperless governance. The initiatives undertaken during the campaign and sustained through August 2026, have further strengthened the Ministry’s commitment to clean, efficient, transparent and environmentally sustainable functioning.

The initiative kicked off with a Preparatory Phase from 15th -30th September, 2025 to identify pending references, review files, and list redundant materials and e-waste. During the campaign, the Ministry achieved 100 per cent disposal of identified public grievances and the pending public grievance appeal, bringing pendency in these categories to zero. In the area of record management, 172 files were weeded out/closed, resulting in better management of records and freeing of valuable office space. Obsolete materials and e-waste were disposed of in accordance with the prescribed environmental guidelines.

The Ministry continued to promote paperless governance through extensive use of digital platforms, including e-Office and e-HRMS. The Ministry also continued its efforts towards wider adoption of the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) by State Legislatures. NeVA facilitates paperless legislative functioning, reduces dependence on physical documents and contributes to greater efficiency and environmental sustainability.

To expedite disposal of pending legislative matters, the Ministry coordinated with Ministries/Departments and State Legislatures for timely action on Parliamentary Assurances, Rule 377 matters and other legislative references. Follow-up communications were also undertaken with State Legislatures to accelerate their transition towards the paperless NeVA platform.

Regular cleanliness drives, inspections and monitoring by senior officers were undertaken to ensure achievement of campaign objectives and sustain the standards established during the campaign. The Ministry also utilised social media platforms to disseminate information on campaign activities and achievements, thereby promoting wider awareness of the objectives of Special Campaign 5.0.

The initiatives undertaken from October 2025 to August 2026 have reinforced the Ministry’s focus on Swachhata, timely disposal of pending matters, effective record management, digital governance, optimal utilisation of office space and environmentally responsible practices, with an emphasis on sustaining these measures as part of regular office functioning.

(Release ID: 2310858)

The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs implemented Special Campaign 5.0 to reinforce Swachhata and digital governance, achieving complete disposal of public grievances and substantial progress in record management and paperless governance from September 2025 through August 2026.

*   **Campaign Period:** Special Campaign 5.0 was conducted from September 2025 to August 2026.
*   **Public Grievances:** 100 percent of identified public grievances were fully disposed of, and the pending public grievance appeal had zero pendency.

headline: BHASHINI, Current AI and Kalpa Impact Conclude VYOMA Innovation Challenge, Showcase Open-Source AI Solutions for India
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

BHASHINI, Current AI and Kalpa Impact Conclude VYOMA Innovation Challenge, Showcase Open-Source AI Solutions for India

Four Innovations were recognised at the Finale Hosted at IIIT-Delhi; 10 Finalist Teams Showcased their Prototypes

16 SEP 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with Current AI and Kalpa Impact, hosted the finale of the VYOMA Innovation Challenge at IIIT-Delhi, bringing together researchers, students and startups developing practical applications of open-source AI hardware for diverse Indian contexts.

The challenge invited participants to build on Suno Sutra, an open-source, multilingual handheld AI reference design co-developed by BHASHINI and Current AI, and explore how AI hardware and software can be adapted for public-interest applications and localised deployment.

The VYOMA Innovation Challenge brought together 10 finalist teams to demonstrate their working prototypes at the finale. The solutions addressed a range of high-impact areas including healthcare, agriculture, welfare access, legal services and accessibility, reflecting the potential of AI designed around India’s diverse needs and real-world constraints.

The finale featured prototype demonstrations by the 10 finalist teams, followed by questions and feedback from the jury. The teams presented their solutions and demonstrated how open-source AI hardware can be adapted to address specific challenges across sectors and communities.

The challenge also brought together the broader ecosystem around open-source AI hardware, multilingual AI and Edge AI, with participants engaging with experts on hardware optimisation, model quantisation, accuracy and pathways for taking promising ideas towards real-world deployment.

Speaking at the finale, Kavita Bhatia, Scientist ‘G’, MeitY, said: “India is moving decisively from being a consumer of global AI to building open, public-interest technologies for its own needs. But the real measure of success is not what works in a laboratory or a pilot, but what works for millions of citizens in the real world. VYOMA brings together open-source hardware and BHASHINI’s language capabilities to take AI closer to the citizen through solutions that can work locally, function offline, reduce bandwidth dependence and protect privacy. By enabling AI to operate on affordable, handheld devices in native languages, this initiative demonstrates how technology can become more personal, accessible and relevant to the last mile.”

Tarun Pandey, Scientist ‘E’, MeitY, said: “Hackathons such as VYOMA provide an important platform for bringing together young innovators, researchers and technology practitioners to develop practical applications of emerging technologies for public good. The initiative reflects BHASHINI’s commitment to fostering innovation, strengthening indigenous AI capabilities and enabling inclusive language technologies that respond to India’s diverse needs. The solutions emerging from the challenge have the potential to contribute to a broader ecosystem of accessible, open and locally relevant AI technologies.”

Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, said:“Language is one part of inclusion, but reaching the last mile is another. VYOMA emerged from the need to explore open, offline hardware that can make AI more inclusive, particularly in diverse and connectivity-constrained environments. What we have seen from these teams is that open hardware can translate into solutions with real-world potential. Today is a milestone, but it is also the beginning of a new journey. The focus now must be on improving these solutions through user feedback, collaboration and the velocity of learning.”

The finale also featured a showcase of the Suno Sutra reference design and discussions on the evolution of the VYOMA Innovation Challenge, the emerging use cases developed by participating teams and the broader potential of open-source AI hardware and embedded AI ecosystems.

Four innovations were recognised as winners of the VYOMA Innovation Challenge. Each winning team received a prize money in recognition of their innovation and potential for public-interest deployment.

The top four winners recognised by the esteemed jury at the VYOMA Innovation Challenge were Team Asha Sahayak, Team Shravan, Team Sangrah – Apna Saathi, and Team Sahyak Mitra – A.V.E.R.A. (Autonomous Voice-enabled Edge Rural Advisor).

The VYOMA Innovation Challenge builds on the vision behind Suno Sutra, unveiled at the India AI Impact Summit in February 2026, to advance open-source, multilingual and human-centric AI hardware. By putting the reference design in the hands of emerging builders, the challenge sought to encourage experimentation and adaptation for diverse environments, use cases and deployment contexts.

Beyond the challenge, VYOMA aims to contribute to an open ecosystem for open-source software and hardware, while advancing multilingual and Edge AI that can be adapted to India’s varied linguistic, technological and deployment environments.

The finale marked a milestone in bringing together innovators, researchers, government stakeholders and ecosystem partners around the development of practical, accessible and locally relevant AI solutions.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is building a national ecosystem for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, powers 800+ government websites, has enabled 9 billion+ cumulative AI inferences and processes 24 million+ AI inferences daily, helping make Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI. National Hub for Language Technology (NHLT) is one of the largest inferencing platforms in the Global South, supporting the growing adoption of Language AI across government and public-facing digital services.

Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma

headline: Institute Finance Committee Reviews Measures to Strengthen Research and Infrastructure at NHRIMH, Kottayam

Institute Finance Committee Reviews Measures to Strengthen Research and Infrastructure at NHRIMH, Kottayam

Committee Reviews Advanced Research, Laboratory Quality, Academic Collaboration and Infrastructure Development

16 SEP 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

The 6th meeting of the Institute Finance Committee (IFC) of the National Homoeopathy Research Institute in Mental Health (NHRIMH), Kottayam, was held on September 14, 2026, under the chairpersonship of Ms. Alarmelmangai D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India.

Ms. Alarmelmangai D. inaugurated the Skill Laboratory for postgraduate students at NHRIMH and visited the OPD and IPD facilities. She interacted with postgraduate students, staff and patients, and reviewed the Institute’s academic, research and patient-care activities.

The Institute Finance Committee (IFC) reviewed key areas relating to the financial, academic, research, infrastructural and administrative development of the Institute. It also reviewed the progress of decisions taken during the previous meeting and considered proposals related to institutional infrastructure, financial management, manpower requirements, academic facilities and research capabilities.

Strengthening the research ecosystem at NHRIMH was identified as a priority, with focus on expanding research programmes, upgrading laboratory infrastructure and developing facilities for advanced experimental and mechanistic research in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

The Committee also reviewed proposals for strengthening institutional capacity in line with the clinical, academic and research requirements of NHRIMH. The Committee encouraged greater collaboration with reputed national and State-level institutions through suitable MoUs to promote academic exchange, research partnerships and capacity building. The Committee also recommended organising a National Conference on World Mental Health Day.

Strengthening the quality of laboratory services was another key area of discussion. The Committee reviewed measures to enhance quality assurance mechanisms and take appropriate steps towards accreditation of laboratory facilities. Measures relating to energy efficiency, safety systems, maintenance and other essential infrastructure requirements were also considered.

The Committee stressed timely completion of approved works through effective coordination and close monitoring, with emphasis on financial prudence, quality and optimal utilisation of resources.

The meeting was attended by Dr. Preetha Kizhakkutil, Adviser (Homoeopathy), Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Subhash Kaushik, Director General, CCRH, New Delhi. The meeting was virtually attended by Dr. Srinivas Rao Chinta, Joint Adviser (Homoeopathy), Ministry of Ayush, Shri Amarendra Singh, Director, Integrated Finance Division (IFD) representative and senior officials of Ministry of Ayush.

The meeting concluded with emphasis on strengthening NHRIMH’s research, academic and clinical capabilities through improved infrastructure, quality laboratory services, institutional collaborations and timely implementation of approved initiatives.

headline: In a major breakthrough, DRI busts huge methamphetamine smuggling syndicate in one of the biggest seizures in North-East Region
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

In a major breakthrough, DRI busts huge methamphetamine smuggling syndicate in one of the biggest seizures in North-East Region

DRI seizes more than 231 kg methamphetamine tablets; Four trucks intercepted; Three arrested

Market value of contraband runs into several hundred crore rupees

16 SEP 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on illicit drug trafficking, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has busted a major drug smuggling syndicate in the North-East, resulting in one of the biggest seizures of methamphetamine in the region. The seizure has an estimated illicit street value running into several hundred crore rupees. The intelligence-led operation involved coordinated surveillance and simultaneous interception at multiple locations, leading to the seizure of a large consignment of methamphetamine.

Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted four trucks at multiple locations in Assam and Tripura during 15.09.2026, which were suspected to be transporting large consignments of methamphetamine tablets.

On 15.09.26, in the first operation, one of the suspected trucks was identified and intercepted at Ramnathpur, Assam, approximately 100 km from Silchar, with the assistance of 38 Battalion, Assam Rifles. Thereafter, the second suspected truck carrying similar consignment was located in the vicinity. However, neither the driver nor the handyman was present with the vehicle.

Rummaging of the first truck resulted in the recovery of 275 packets, weighing 55 kg in total, containing pinkish-orangish tablets, suspected to be methamphetamine tablets, concealed in the roof of the driver's cabin. Detailed rummaging of the second truck resulted in the recovery of 271 packets of similarly coloured tablets, weighing 54.2 kg also concealed in the roof of the driver's cabin. A total of 109.2 kg suspected methamphetamine tablets, were recovered and seized along with two vehicles under the provisions of the NDPS Act and one person was arrested.

Simultaneously, as part of the same intelligence-led operation, another targeted goods carrier carrying a declared load of cement was identified while proceeding from Khowai towards Agartala and intercepted at Teliamura, approximately 45 km from Agartala, with the assistance of 28 Battalion, Assam Rifles. Detailed examination of resulted in the recovery of 295 plastic packets, containing 72.6 kg pinkish-orangish tablets suspected to be methamphetamine, concealed in the roof of the driver’s cabin. The contraband and vehicle were seized and the driver was arrested.

Further intelligence developed during the operation and prompt action by DRI officers led to the interception of another truck belonging to the same syndicate near Panisagar, Tripura. Search of the vehicle resulted in the recovery of 50 kg suspected methamphetamine tablets, also concealed in the vehicle. The contraband and vehicle were seized and the driver was arrested.

The coordinated action of DRI resulted in the seizure of a total of 231.8 kg of suspected methamphetamine tablets, and the arrest of three persons. All four trucks used for transportation of the contraband have also been seized.

Earlier, in the month of August 2026, DRI in two intelligence-led operations carried out near Silchar and Mizoram had seized 76 kg methamphetamine tablets, which were also found concealed in the vehicles at different places.

(Release ID: 2310841)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has busted a major drug smuggling syndicate in North-East India, executing a coordinated intelligence-led operation on September 15, 2026, that resulted in one of the region's largest seizures of methamphetamine. The operation spanned multiple locations in Assam and Tripura, leading to the seizure of over 231 kg of contraband valued at several hundred crore rupees, the arrest of three suspects, and the confiscation of four transport trucks.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
* **Total Seizure:** 231.8 kg of suspected pinkish-orangish methamphetamine tablets recovered across four intercepted trucks.
* **Estimated Value:** The illicit street value of the contraband runs into several hundred crore rupees.
* **Operation Date:** Interceptions took place on September 15, 2026 (15.09.2026).
* **Arrests and Confiscations:** Three individuals were arrested, and all four trucks used for transporting the drugs were seized under the provisions of the NDPS Act.
* **Concealment Method:** The methamphetamine tablets were primarily concealed within the roofs of the drivers' cabins of the vehicles.
* **Interception Details:**
  * **Assam Operation (Ramnathpur, ~100 km from Silchar):** Two trucks intercepted with the assistance of the 38 Battalion, Assam Rifles. A total of 109.2 kg of tablets (55 kg from the first truck, 54.2 kg from the second) was recovered, and one person was arrested.
  * **Tripura Operation 1 (Teliamura, ~45 km from Agartala):** A truck carrying a declared load of cement was intercepted with the assistance of the 28 Battalion, Assam Rifles, yielding 72.6 kg of tablets; the driver was arrested.
  * **Tripura Operation 2 (Panisagar):** A follow-up intelligence operation led to the interception of a fourth truck, resulting in the recovery of 50 kg of tablets and the arrest of the driver.
* **Previous Operations:** The release notes that in August 2026, the DRI had previously seized 76 kg of methamphetamine tablets in two separate operations near Silchar and Mizoram.
* **Release Information:** Issued by PIB Delhi on September 16, 2026, under Release ID 2310841.

headline: CBIC commemorates 10 years of India’s Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) Programme; Outlines way forward and reaffirms commitment to trusted trade
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

CBIC commemorates 10 years of India’s Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) Programme; Outlines way forward and reaffirms commitment to trusted trade

AEO Programme is pivotal in transforming India’s customs administration into a modern, trusted and facilitative system aligned with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards: CBIC Chairman

CBIC Member (Customs) noted transformation of Customs from a transaction-centric approach to a risk-based and trust-oriented model of administration since the introduction of the current AEO framework

16 SEP 2026 3:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) today celebrated a decade of India’s Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) Programme with a commemorative event titled “AEO@10: Accelerating Growth, Enhancing Trust, Optimizing Trade” in New Delhi.

The event brought together policymakers, industry leaders, logistics stakeholders, WCO experts and Authorised Economic Operators to reflect on the programme’s achievements and chart the roadmap for its future.

Addressing the gathering as Chief Guest, Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, underscored the pivotal role played by the AEO Programme in transforming India’s customs administration into a modern, trusted and facilitative system aligned with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards.

He noted that the programme has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s trade facilitation architecture by promoting voluntary compliance, strengthening supply chain security and enabling faster, more predictable cross-border movement of goods. The CBIC Chairman outlined five big ideas for the next decade:

technology-driven facilitation

radical inclusivity for MSMEs

seamless inter-agency coordination

global leadership through expanded Mutual Recognition Arrangements, and

synergy across indirect tax verticals

Highlighting CBIC’s commitment to stakeholder-centric reforms, the Chairman announced the launch of a structured feedback response form on the AEO portal to enable continuous and systematic inputs from AEO entities and other stakeholders.

Drawing on Pillar 2 of the WCO SAFE Framework and the CBIC Citizens’ Charter, he emphasised that trade is an equal partner in building a trusted ecosystem and that feedback must be continuous. He also referred to the Eligible Manufacturer Importer (EMI) Scheme, highlighted by the Union Finance Minister’s in the Union Budget speech, as an important stepping stone that rewards early compliance and creates a natural pathway to higher AEO tiers.

In his address, Member (Customs), CBIC, recalled the transformation of Customs from a transaction-centric approach to a risk-based and trust-oriented model of administration since the introduction of the current AEO framework through Circular No. 33/2016-Customs. He underlined that voluntary compliance promotes good governance, reduces supply-chain risk and transaction costs, and that supply-chain security remains central to the resilience of India’s trade ecosystem. He noted that important discussions at the annual Customs Consultative Group meeting held in Kolkata, together with representations from trade, have informed several trade-friendly process improvements now under consideration. These include a unified Standard Operating Procedure for uniform processing across zones; a clear checklist for applicants and Zonal AEO Programme Managers; a single-deficiency approach; time-bound processing; copying of deficiency communications to the applicant; a clarified position on financial solvency; and strengthening of dedicated Client Relationship Managers and trained validators, in line with the National Trade Facilitation Action Plan.

The Member (Customs) also stated that, in the same spirit of reducing compliance burden, documentation requirements under the EMI Scheme have already been rationalised through Circular No. 39/2026-Customs dated 3rd September 2026, bringing down the documents to be uploaded from ten to three, with effect from 15th September 2026.

The event marked the launch of the commemorative publication “A Decade of AEO in India: Celebrating Trusted Trade Partnerships”, documenting the evolution, milestones and impact of India’s AEO Programme over the past ten years, and incorporating contributions from CBIC officers, international partners, trade and industry. A stakeholder feedback survey on the AEO Programme was also announced to obtain structured inputs from industry for guiding future reforms. In addition, new AEO certificates were presented to select businesses, recognising their commitment to secure and compliant international trade.

In her welcome address earlier, Dr. Kavita Bhatnagar, Principal Commissioner and National AEO Programme Manager, highlighted the remarkable growth of the programme since its inception and emphasised the importance of continued collaboration between Customs and the trade community in building a trusted and resilient trading environment.

Representatives from leading industry bodies, including the Federation of Freight Forwarders’ Associations in India (FFFAI), appreciated the significant contribution of the AEO Programme towards improving ease of doing business, reducing transaction costs and enhancing supply chain predictability. Leading AEO entities also shared their experiences, highlighting tangible benefits such as expedited customs clearance, improved operational efficiency and strengthened global business confidence.

India’s AEO Programme has, over the past decade, become an important pillar of CBIC’s trade facilitation initiatives by rewarding compliant businesses with simplified customs procedures and risk-based facilitation while maintaining robust supply chain security. As of date, 5,967 entities — comprising importers, exporters, manufacturers, customs brokers, logistics operators and warehouse operators — have been certified under the AEO Programme across T1, T2, T3 and LO categories.

The programme has steadily expanded its coverage of the logistics chain, digitised application processes, established dedicated AEO Cells, and introduced special facilitative provisions for MSMEs. As India continues to expand its engagement with trusted trading partners across the world, CBIC remains committed to further strengthening the AEO Programme through stakeholder-centric reforms, technology adoption, international cooperation and continuous feedback from trade, thereby contributing to the objectives of Viksit Bharat @2047 and making India an increasingly preferred destination for global trade and investment.

headline: India reaffirms Commitment to Ozone Layer Protection and Climate Action at 32nd World Ozone Day Celebration in Mumbai
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

India reaffirms Commitment to Ozone Layer Protection and Climate Action at 32nd World Ozone Day Celebration in Mumbai

The Country has exceeded its Montreal Protocol commitments without compromising Development: MoS (EFCC) Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh

Maharashtra working towards Prime Minister's vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 through Sustainable Development: State Environment Minister Smt. Pankaja Munde

India’s Net Zero Portal and NAPCC Dashboard launched on World Ozone Day 2026

248 ITIs adopted by 12 Refrigeration and Airconditioning (RAC) Manufacturers; To align Training of next generation of Technicians with Industry Standards

16 SEP 2026 3:11PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change today organised the national celebration of the 32nd World Ozone Day in Mumbai, with the theme ‘Global Action for a Cooler Planet’. The event was presided over by Union Minister of State for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, along with Maharashtra State Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Smt. Pankaja Munde.

The event was also graced by the presence of Secretary (EFCC), Shri Tanmay Kumar; Ms. Angela Lusigi, Country Head (UNDP); Ms. Ulrike Ebeling, Country Director and Head (GIZ India), besides senior officials from Governments of India and Maharashtra, besides representatives of international organisations, industry representatives, academic experts and school children to highlight India’s efforts towards protection of the ozone layer and a cooler and more sustainable planet.

On the occasion, the dignitaries launched India's Net Zero Portal and the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) Dashboard. The Net Zero portal will serve as a central repository to track, coordinate and showcase India’s climate commitments and enable industries, organisations and government bodies to voluntarily register and display their progress towards net-zero emissions. Further, the NAPCC Portal was also launched as a centralised digital gateway showcasing India’s overarching National Action Plan on Climate Change, with tracking and insights across national missions. (Press Release: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2310737®=48&lang=2)

Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh said India has demonstrated that economic growth and environmental protection can go hand in hand. The Minister said India has shown proactive leadership in conservation and has met its commitments under the Montreal Protocol without compromising development. He emphasised that collective action involving governments, scientists, industry, officers and citizens is essential to address environmental challenges.

Shri Singh highlighted Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) as a framework for translating environmental protection into simple, everyday actions. The Minister said mindful utilisation of natural resources, instead of wasteful consumption, can enable citizens to contribute to environmental conservation. He urged citizens to adopt three measures for sustainable cooling: get air-conditioners serviced by certified and skilled technicians who handle refrigerants safely; set AC temperatures at a comfortable level, preferably around 24 degrees Celsius, to save electricity and reduce carbon emissions; and choose high star-rated, energy-efficient appliances using climate-friendly refrigerants.

Smt. Munde said Maharashtra is working towards Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision for a developed India by 2047, with a focus on decarbonisation, sustainable development and environment-friendly growth. She said Maharashtra is preparing roadmaps and action plans to integrate ozone-layer protection and climate action, while also advancing energy-efficient and climate-responsive cooling systems and buildings, particularly in view of the State’s rapid urbanisation and rising temperatures.

UNDP Country Head Ms. Angela Lusigi said India’s implementation of the Montreal Protocol demonstrates that economic growth and environmental protection can advance together. Highlighting India’s progress in phasing out ozone-depleting substances, she said the country’s targets have often been achieved ahead of schedule, while promoting low-impact technologies, strengthening small and medium enterprises and training technicians in new refrigerants, creating opportunities for green jobs.

GIZ Country Director and Head Ms. Ulrike Ebeling said that India and Germany are working together to advance climate-friendly cooling solutions and support implementation of the HCFC Phase-out Management Plan Stage III (2025–2030), with a focus on the refrigeration and air-conditioning servicing sector. She highlighted efforts to establish a nationally recognised certification system for air-conditioning technicians, with a target to train 25,000 technicians by 2030, besides strengthening training capacity in the cooling sector.

The event also witnessed the announcement of the adoption of 248 Industrial Training Institutions by 12 Refrigeration and Airconditioning (RAC) manufacturers through a 4-Party Memorandum of Agreement comprising RAC manufacturers, Ozone Cell, Regional Directorate, Directorate General of Training (DGT) and State Directorate, DGT. The initiative is aimed at strengthening training infrastructure for the next generation of technicians. The institutional partnership aims to align classroom learning with industry standards. This synergy will build a workforce skilled in eco-friendly, low-global-warming-potential (GWP) technologies, directly supporting India’s commitments under the Montreal Protocol and the India Cooling Action Plan (ICAP).

Publications based on studies conducted by the Ozone Cell, MoEF&CC were released on the occasion. The event also featured the announcement of winners of a national school-level poster and slogan writing competitions, as well as winners of a national online quiz competition. A video film showcasing India’s proactive industrial transformation and pioneering strides towards a cooler, more sustainable planet was also screened.

India has been a Party to the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer and the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer and all its amendments since 1992. The country has met all its commitments under the Montreal Protocol schedule for different ozone-depleting substances. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), Carbon tetrachloride (CTC) and Halons have already been phased out for controlled applications, while India is currently phasing out Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) as per the accelerated phase-out schedule of the Montreal Protocol. India has already met the 2015, 2020 and 2025 phase-out targets for HCFCs.

India ratified the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol in September 2021. The Kigali Amendment came into force for India on 26 December 2021. As per the agreed phase-down schedule, India will complete the phase-down of HFC production and consumption in four steps from 2032 onwards, with reductions of 10 per cent in 2032, 20 per cent in 2037, 30 per cent in 2042 and 85 per cent in 2047, against the baseline.

headline: Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month
fullText:
Ministry of Labour & Employment

Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month

Over 51 lakh additional employees expected to come under mandatory EPFO coverage

Decision strengthens formalisation and advances India’s long-term social security vision

Major step towards stronger retirement security and Viksit Bharat@2047

16 SEP 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Ministry of Labour & Employment to enhance the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month. The decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers.

The EPFO wage ceiling remained unchanged throughout the decade from 2004 to 2014, before being substantially enhanced to Rs.15,000 in September 2014. The present decision carries forward this approach by further raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 to reflect the sustained wage growth, rising incomes and a continued expansion of formal employment over the intervening years.

At present, a fresh employee joining employment at a wage above Rs.15,000 per month is not automatically covered under the EPF framework and may remain outside mandatory provident fund, pension and associated insurance protection. Raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 will bring a substantial segment of employees in the Rs.15,000– Rs.25,000 wage band within the statutory social security framework.

The approval will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI), in accordance with the applicable scheme provisions. It will also enable the statutory contribution and pensionable-wage framework to better reflect prevailing wage levels.

Since the wage ceiling was last revised in September 2014, India has witnessed sustained wage growth, rising incomes and continued expansion of formal employment. In several States and occupations, minimum wages have also moved closer to the existing threshold. The enhancement to Rs.25,000 therefore updates the EPFO framework in line with rising wage levels and extends the benefits of formal social security to a wider segment of the workforce.

The measure is expected to give a further impetus to formalisation of employment, worker retention and long-term retirement security. By bringing a larger number of employees automatically within the statutory social security framework, the decision strengthens the principle that formal employment should be accompanied by portable and assured social security protection. For employers as well, wider social security coverage can support employee retention, workforce stability, morale and the development of a more secure and future-ready workforce.

The proposal underwent detailed inter-ministerial consultations and was recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee in its meeting held on 16 June 2026. The annual Government outgo is estimated at about Rs.11,339 crore, against the existing annual budgetary support of about Rs.10,250 crore. The estimated expenditure over five years is approximately Rs.56,696 crore.

EPFO today operates one of the world’s largest social security systems, administering the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI). The latest EPFO data show around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners. EDLI provides insurance protection linked to EPF membership.

India’s workforce is at the heart of its growth story. As wages rise, incomes improve and formal employment expands, the Government’s continued emphasis on employment generation and formalisation is creating new opportunities for workers. The enhancement of the EPFO wage ceiling ensures that the social security framework also keeps pace with this progress and that a larger number of workers in formal employment receive statutory social security protection.

This approval marks another important step towards building an inclusive, resilient and future-ready social security architecture, ensuring that social protection advances alongside economic growth, rising wages and expanding formal employment as India moves towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

The Ministry of Labour & Employment and EPFO will undertake the necessary statutory and administrative steps for implementation of the decision.

The enhancement to Rs.25,000 therefore updates the EPFO framework in line with rising wage levels and extends the benefits of formal social security to a wider segment of the workforce.

The measure is expected to give a further impetus to formalisation of employment, worker retention and long-term retirement security. By bringing a larger number of employees automatically within the statutory social security framework, the decision strengthens the principle that formal employment should be accompanied by portable and assured social security protection. For employers as well, wider social security coverage can support employee retention, workforce stability, morale and the development of a more secure and future-ready workforce.

The proposal underwent detailed inter-ministerial consultations and was recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee in its meeting held on 16 June 2026. The annual Government outgo is estimated at about Rs.11,339 crore, against the existing annual budgetary support of about Rs.10,250 crore. The estimated expenditure over five years is approximately Rs.56,696 crore.

EPFO today operates one of the world’s largest social security systems, administering the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI). The latest EPFO data show around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners. EDLI provides insurance protection linked to EPF membership.

India’s workforce is at the heart of its growth story. As wages rise, incomes improve and formal employment expands, the Government’s continued emphasis on employment generation and formalisation is creating new opportunities for workers. The enhancement of the EPFO wage ceiling ensures that the social security framework also keeps pace with this progress and that a larger number of workers in formal employment receive statutory social security protection.

This approval marks another important step towards building an inclusive, resilient and future-ready social security architecture, ensuring that social protection advances alongside economic growth, rising wages and expanding formal employment as India moves towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

The Ministry of Labour & Employment and EPFO will undertake the necessary statutory and administrative steps for implementation of the decision.

headline: Shri Rajiv Gauba Calls Electric Mobility a "Strategic Imperative" for Viksit Bharat as NITI Aayog Launches Second Edition of India Electric Mobility Index
fullText:
Shri Rajiv Gauba Calls Electric Mobility a "Strategic Imperative" for Viksit Bharat as NITI Aayog Launches Second Edition of India Electric Mobility Index

16 SEP 2026 2:50PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Rajiv Gauba, in his address at the NITI Aayog Workshop on State EV Policies, where the second edition of the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) report was launched, highlighted that the global transition to electric mobility is well underway.

In 2025, he noted, electric cars accounted for around one-tenth of new car sales in the US, more than a quarter in the EU, and over half in China and that these shares are expected to rise significantly across the world in the years ahead. He pointed to the recent West Asia crisis, noting that it could become a major inflection point for electric mobility, much as the oil crises of the 1970s accelerated the global push towards greater fuel efficiency.

Describing the shift as “an economic, environmental, and strategic imperative” for the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, he highlighted India’s dependence on imports for nearly 89% of its crude oil requirements, a dependence that is likely to increase as car ownership rises from current levels if EVs are not adopted more widely. He noted that the automotive sector contributes around 7.1% of GDP and supports nearly 1.9 crore jobs, underscoring the importance of keeping the sector aligned with the global transition to electric vehicles. He also highlighted the significant public health costs of vehicular emissions in cities such as Delhi, making the transition to cleaner mobility an urgent priority.

He outlined the scale of government support already in place, totalling over ₹92,000 crore, through schemes such as FAME, PM E-DRIVE and PM E-bus Sewa, as well as two production-linked incentive schemes for Automobiles & Auto Components and for Advanced Chemistry Cell battery storage.

He also highlighted the rapid expansion of the EV charging ecosystem, with oil marketing companies and private players driving the development of charging infrastructure. The newly launched Unified Bharat e-Charge app is expected to further strengthen this ecosystem by making charging infrastructure more accessible and convenient for users.

Turning to States, he noted that 29 of India's 36 States and Union Territories have now notified EV policies, with IEMI scores showing broad-based improvement; the highest State score rising from 77 to 84 and the median score from 36 to 40 over the past year.

He noted that the Index offers a data-driven framework to help states monitor their progress and formulate evidence-based policies. He also emphasized that the differences between States experience in E-Mobility due to differing strategies, shaped by their own industrial base, fiscal capacity and geography are not a complication, but a strength, provided states learn from each other. He urged States to prioritise electrifying public transport in select cities, ensure charging infrastructure is spatially well-distributed and reliable, and promote investments in research and innovation.

headline: Government Eases RCMC Requirement for Export Consignments up to ₹3 Lakh
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Government Eases RCMC Requirement for Export Consignments up to ₹3 Lakh

RCMC Exemption Lowers Entry Barriers for MSMEs and First-Time Exporters

16 SEP 2026 2:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has introduced a de minimis exemption from the requirement of Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC) or Certificate of Registration for small-value export consignments up to ₹3 lakh. The measure is aimed at reducing the compliance burden for new and small exporters and facilitating exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels.

The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has amended Para 2.57 of the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023 to provide that RCMC or Certificate of Registration will not be required for export consignments having a Free-on-Board (FOB) value of up to ₹3 lakh, wherever such certificate is otherwise required under the Foreign Trade Policy. Export consignments exceeding ₹3 lakh will continue to require a valid RCMC or Certificate of Registration, wherever applicable.

Historical data for the last five years (2021-22 to 2025-26) indicates that low-value exports account for a significant share of shipping bills but a very small proportion of the overall export value. Consignments up to USD 3,000, for instance, account for 43 per cent of shipping bills but only 0.86 per cent of India’s total merchandise export value. The exemption is therefore expected to cover a substantial number of small-value export transactions while having only a marginal impact on the overall value of exports.

At present, exporters are generally required to obtain an RCMC or Certificate of Registration from the relevant Export Promotion Council or Commodity Board, wherever applicable under the Foreign Trade Policy. For new or occasional exporters undertaking small-value consignments, this involves an additional compliance step, including identifying the appropriate registering body, submitting the prescribed documents and completing the registration process before undertaking exports.

The measure provides MSMEs, artisans, small businesses and first-time exporters with a simpler entry point into international markets by removing the requirement to obtain an RCMC upfront for eligible small-value consignments. This will enable emerging exporters to test overseas markets and establish an export track record with lower initial compliance requirements.

As exporters expand their operations and their consignments move beyond the ₹3 lakh threshold, they can obtain membership of the relevant Export Promotion Councils or Commodity Boards and access export promotion, market access and other institutional support services.

The measure offers lower entry barriers for new exporters, enabling first-time and occasional exporters to undertake eligible small-value exports without obtaining an RCMC upfront. It is particularly beneficial for MSMEs and small businesses, as small manufacturers, artisans, entrepreneurs and emerging exporters will be able to explore overseas markets and build an export track record with lower initial compliance requirements.

The exemption will also facilitate e-commerce and other emerging export channels. It is expected to support low-value exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels that are increasingly enabling businesses to reach international customers.

The measure will support the gradual integration of emerging exporters into global markets. As exporters scale up and undertake higher-value consignments, they can obtain RCMC membership and access the wider range of export promotion and institutional support provided through Export Promotion Councils and other prescribed bodies.

At the same time, the existing framework for larger exports remains unchanged. The exemption is limited to small-value consignments, while the requirement of RCMC or Certificate of Registration will continue for consignments exceeding ₹3 lakh, wherever otherwise applicable.

The measure will also help broaden the base of Export Promotion Councils and Commodity Boards by encouraging greater participation of MSMEs in exports. By lowering the initial compliance barrier, more MSMEs will be able to enter international markets and, as their export operations scale beyond the ₹3 lakh threshold, obtain RCMC and become members of the relevant EPCs or Commodity Boards to access export promotion activities, market access initiatives and other institutional support.

The measure reinforces the Government’s commitment to reducing the compliance burden, broadening participation in exports and making international trade more accessible to MSMEs, first-time exporters and emerging businesses.

headline: Union MoS Raksha Khadse chairs district review meetings in Saitual and Kolasib; reviews development priorities, sports and youth engagement
fullText:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

Union MoS Raksha Khadse chairs district review meetings in Saitual and Kolasib; reviews development priorities, sports and youth engagement

Focus on grassroots sports, youth mobilisation, substance-abuse prevention, agriculture, connectivity and effective implementation of Central Government schemes

16 SEP 2026 2:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports, Smt. Raksha Khadse, chaired district-level review meetings for Saitual and Kolasib during her official visit to Mizoram on 15–16 September 2026. The meetings reviewed key development priorities, implementation of Central Government schemes, sports infrastructure, youth engagement, agriculture, connectivity, healthcare and livelihood opportunities.

SAITUAL: YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, AGRICULTURE AND SPORTS

In Saitual, the review meeting was attended by District Collector Shri Shriniwas Sadi, Superintendent of Police Shri Vivek Kumar Maurya, senior district officials and representatives of sports federations and community organisations.

A key focus of the meeting was substance-abuse prevention among youth. Smt. Khadse emphasised the importance of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan and called for stronger coordination among youth groups, community organisations and law-enforcement agencies. She stressed the importance of peer-led awareness, constructive youth engagement and sustained community-level efforts to prevent substance abuse.

The meeting also reviewed the district’s agriculture and horticulture potential, with emphasis on improving market access and supply linkages for Mizoram’s organic produce so that local farmers can connect more effectively with wider markets.

Representatives of local sports federations highlighted ground-level requirements relating to sports infrastructure and athlete development. Smt. Khadse emphasised that infrastructure must be complemented by regular coaching, structured training and sustained athlete support to help young sportspersons progress to higher levels of competition. She also highlighted the role of the Khelo India Scheme in expanding sporting opportunities at the grassroots.

KOLASIB: CONNECTIVITY, HEALTHCARE AND LIVELIHOODS

For Kolasib, Smt. Khadse chaired a district review meeting attended by Shri H. Dolianbuaia, MCS, District Collector; Pu Lalrinpuia Varte, Superintendent of Police, and senior administrative officers and heads of departments.

Road connectivity emerged as a key infrastructure priority, with discussions focusing on improving access to markets, essential services and economic opportunities for local communities.

The Minister also reviewed the functioning of the district’s Community Health Centre, five Primary Health Centres and nursing school, with emphasis on optimal utilisation of existing healthcare infrastructure.

Agriculture received detailed attention, particularly the role of the Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) in supporting farmers. Kolasib has more than 10,000 active farmers, while the KVK currently provides technical guidance to over 5,000 growers and facilitates inter-state internships and visiting faculty programmes.

The review also covered the cooperative sector, including 102 functioning cooperatives, largely agriculture-oriented, as well as the Janaushadhi Kendra, with discussions focusing on their potential to strengthen local livelihoods and community-level economic activity.

BOOSTING LOCAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP

Smt. Khadse reviewed the implementation of the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) in the district. Discussions focused on resolving portal-access issues that had affected sanctions during 2025–26 and expediting support for 25 identified local enterprises, including furniture workshops, grocery stores and mineral-water units.

While reviewing the Public Distribution System and Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, Smt. Khadse directed officials to address beneficiary-data gaps and ensure accurate records so that all eligible households receive the intended benefits.

STRENGTHENING GRASSROOTS SPORTS IN KOLASIB

Sports emerged as an important area of discussion in the Kolasib review. Football, hockey and wrestling were identified among the prominent sporting disciplines in the district. Athletes from Kolasib are participating in national-level football leagues, while the district also has a hockey ground and has produced a national-level hockey player.

The need for a dedicated training centre was discussed to provide local athletes with structured coaching and sustained training opportunities.

Smt. Khadse also reviewed sports infrastructure being developed under the VB-GRAM-G initiative, including football and volleyball grounds and maintenance of existing facilities. She suggested that sports grounds under the initiative should be developed across the district’s 51 villages, enabling young people to access sporting facilities closer to their communities.

MY BHARAT AND YOUTH MOBILISATION

Youth mobilisation and substance-abuse prevention were also discussed in detail. The Superintendent of Police briefed the Minister on the district’s Nasha Mukt initiatives, with emphasis on awareness and preventive interventions.

Smt. Khadse stressed the importance of channelising the energy of young people towards sports, education, community service and constructive social engagement. She called for greater awareness activities in educational institutions and highlighted the importance of positive peer influence in reaching young people.

The District Youth Officer informed the meeting that around 9,000 youth are registered on the MY Bharat platform in Kolasib. Smt. Khadse called for greater mobilisation of MY Bharat volunteers for awareness activities and stronger coordination between MY Bharat volunteers and the Police Department.

FOCUS ON GRASSROOTS DEVELOPMENT

Across both district reviews, Smt. Raksha Khadse emphasised that India’s youth are central to the country’s development journey and that their energy and potential must be channelled into sports, education, entrepreneurship, community engagement and productive livelihoods.

She highlighted the need to strengthen grassroots sporting ecosystems, particularly in regions such as Mizoram with strong sporting potential, by ensuring access to facilities, quality coaching, structured training and appropriate support systems.

Smt. Khadse also stressed that effective implementation of government programmes requires accurate data, stronger inter-departmental coordination and continuous engagement with local communities. She emphasised that Central Government schemes must translate into tangible opportunities and improved outcomes for beneficiaries at the grassroots.

The district reviews concluded with an emphasis on stronger coordination among district administrations, police authorities, youth institutions, sports bodies, agricultural institutions, cooperatives and community organisations to advance inclusive development and create greater opportunities for the people and youth of Saitual and Kolasib.

Ministry of Jal Shakti

Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation launches Swachh Seva Aankalan for Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen)

Gram Panchayat-level annual digital self-assessment framework for assessment of rural sanitation service delivery

Gram Sabha validation to strengthen community participation, transparency and accountability

16 SEP 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil launched Swachh Seva Aankalan (SSA) on 15th September 2026 during a virtual meeting with States/UTs. The meeting was attended by the Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna. Ministers in charge of Rural Sanitation and concerned officials and Mission Directors of Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) from States/UTs joined virtually.

Swachh Seva Aankalan (SSA) is an annual, Gram Panchayat level digital self-assessment framework developed by Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) 2.0 for assessment and monitoring of sanitation service delivery in rural areas. This multi-tier evaluation framework envisages the involvement of Gram Panchayats, Gram Sabhas, Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSC), District and State/UT level officials for strengthening sanitation service delivery at grass root level.

Under SSA, ODF Plus (Model) declared Gram Panchayats, together with their VWSCs and local communities, will assess the status of ODF sustainability, visual cleanliness and Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) in the Gram Panchayat. The functionality and Operation & Maintenance (O&M) status of sanitation and community SLWM assets will also be self-assessed through the Aankalan. The findings will be discussed and validated by the concerned Gram Sabha and will be available to the District and State/UT authorities to be reviewed in DWSM/SWSM meetings. These authorities will be able to identify service delivery gaps and prepare their respective improvement plans for corrective action at grassroot level.

In the spirit of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, this will further empower the Gram Panchayats and Gram Sabhas to review their achievements and progress and make focused efforts for improvement in the same.

headline: PMAY-U: The Story of Housing, Inclusion and Empowerment
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

PMAY-U: The Story of Housing, Inclusion and Empowerment

16 SEP 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi

PMAY-U is a flagship urban housing mission aimed at ensuring Housing for All in urban areas. It provides pucca houses with basic civic amenities to eligible urban households across the country. The Mission primarily targets EWS, LIG, MIG families and slum dwellers in cities and towns. Implementation experience under PMAY-U led to the launch of a restructured PMAY-U 2.0 in 2024. Strong emphasis is placed on inclusivity, with benefits extended to women and other vulnerable urban groups. Technology-enabled systems such as geo-tagging and real-time dashboards have strengthened transparency and monitoring.

The Foundation of Urban Aspiration

A safe and secure home is the foundation of a dignified life. It provides families with stability, protection, and the confidence to pursue better opportunities. Access to quality housing not only improves living conditions but also contributes to better health, education, financial security, and overall well-being. For millions of urban families, a permanent home represents more than shelter; it is a pathway to a brighter and more secure future.

Recognising the transformative role of housing in fostering inclusive growth, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Urban (PMAY-U) was launched in June 2015. The Mission places affordable housing at the centre of urban development. Over the years, it has evolved the housing landscape through scale, innovation, and a focus on those who need support the most.

PMAY-U: A National Response to Urban Housing Needs

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Urban (PMAY-U) provides all-weather pucca houses with basic civic amenities to eligible urban households across the country. It focuses on the housing needs of slum dwellers and families belonging to the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Low Income Groups (LIG), and Middle-Income Groups (MIG). Under the scheme, central assistance is provided to States and Union Territories for the construction and delivery of affordable housing. The original mission period was up to March 2022. However, on the request of States/UTs and to ensure the completion of sanctioned projects, the scheme period has been extended until 30th September 2026. Further, based on the learnings and experiences from implementation of PMAY-U and owing to the increase in housing demand, the scheme was revamped and launched as PMAY-U 2.0 in September 2024. The scheme continues the vision of “Housing for All” in urban areas with a more responsive and inclusive approach.

Who is a beneficiary family?

A beneficiary family under PMAY-U includes a husband, wife, and unmarried sons and/or unmarried daughters. The family should not own a pucca house (an all-weather dwelling unit) anywhere in India in any member’s name. An adult earning member, regardless of marital status, is considered a separate household. This applies only if:

He or she does not own a pucca house in his/her name anywhere in India.

In a married couple, either spouse or both jointly can avail a single house. This is subject to household income eligibility under the scheme. An eligible beneficiary can avail benefits under only one of the Mission’s four verticals.

Individuals with a pucca house below 21 sq. m. can be considered for upgradation with expansion of up to 30 sq. m. under the scheme. If this is not feasible due to land or other constraints, she/he can get a house under PMAY(U) elsewhere.

PMAY – Urban 2.0: Building the Next Chapter

PMAY-U 2.0 marks the next phase of India's affordable housing mission, building on the strong foundation laid by PMAY-U. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to 1 crore additional urban poor and middle-class families and is being implemented from 2024 to 2029. Under the scheme, eligible families receive financial assistance of up to ₹2.50 lakh per unit to support the construction or purchase of affordable houses in urban areas. PMAY-U 2.0 also supports the provision of affordable rental housing for eligible beneficiaries, helping address diverse housing needs across urban India.

The PMAY-U 2.0 scheme is open to families belonging to EWS, LIG, and MIG segments. The income criteria for beneficiaries is as follows:

EWS households: Annual income up to ₹3 lakh.

LIG households: Annual income from ₹3 lakh to ₹6 lakh.

MIG households: Annual income from ₹6 lakh to ₹9 lakh.

Four Verticals of PMAY-U 2.0

Building on the experience of PMAY-U, PMAY-U 2.0 adopts a similar four-pronged approach to address diverse housing needs in urban India.

Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC)

The BLC vertical provides financial assistance of up to ₹2.5 lakh to eligible EWS families. They can construct new pucca houses on their own available land, with a maximum carpet area of 45 sqm.

Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP)

The AHP vertical provides financial assistance to EWS beneficiaries for owning a pucca house. Public or private agencies construct affordable houses with 30–45 sqm carpet area for eligible beneficiaries. Financial assistance of up to ₹2.5 lakh per unit is provided together by Central and State Governments towards the property's purchase price.

Affordable Rental Housing (ARH)

The ARH vertical provides affordable, dignified and hygienic rental housing for urban dwellers needing short-term accommodation or for those who are unable to buy or construct houses. It covers EWS and LIG beneficiaries, including migrants, homeless, industrial workers, working women, construction workers, urban poor and destitute persons. It also covers street vendors, rickshaw pullers, contractual employees among others. Essential infrastructure, including water, sewerage or septage, sanitation, internal roads, health centres, etc., is also addressed to make the houses livable.

Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS)

The ISS vertical provides interest subsidy on eligible home loans under PMAY-U 2.0. It covers loans sanctioned and disbursed on or after 1st September 2024. Eligible EWS, LIG and MIG beneficiaries can avail the subsidy for purchase, repurchase or construction of houses. A maximum interest subsidy of ₹1.80 is provided to eligible beneficiaries having a loan tenure of more than five years.

Key Achievements of PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0

The journey of PMAY-U reflects a sustained commitment to making affordable housing accessible at scale. Between 2005 and 2014, only about 8 lakh urban houses were completed under earlier schemes. As on 9th August 2026, 1.25 crore houses have been sanctioned across PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0. Of these, more than 1 crore houses have been completed and delivered to beneficiaries across the country.

Ensuring Equitable Access to Urban Housing

The true success of urban development lies in how widely its benefits are shared. The Mission places inclusivity at the centre of its approach, supporting vulnerable households across cities and towns.

Women have remained at the heart of this transformation. PMAY-U mandates ownership or co-ownership of houses in the name of women beneficiaries. This provision has strengthened financial security and enhanced their role in household decision-making.

The Mission also prioritises housing access for SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and transgender persons. By addressing the needs of diverse beneficiary groups, PMAY-U has helped make urban growth more equitable and accessible.

PMAY-U 2.0 continues this commitment through targeted support for diverse beneficiary groups. As on 9th August 2026, about 18.38 lakh houses have been sanctioned under the scheme. It combines home ownership opportunities with focused interventions for vulnerable communities.

Of the 18.38 lakh houses sanctioned, 14.40 lakh houses fall under the Beneficiary-Led Construction vertical.

2.48 lakh houses have been sanctioned under the Affordable Housing in Partnership vertical.

1.36 lakh houses have been covered under the Interest Subsidy Scheme vertical.

13,046 dwelling units have been sanctioned under the Affordable Rental Housing component.

Among the 1.25 crore houses sanctioned under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, 1 crore houses have been allotted to women (in the name of female head of the household or in joint ownership).

These achievements reflect the Mission's continued focus on ensuring that housing benefits reach those most in need. By combining affordability with inclusion, PMAY-U is helping create more equitable and resilient urban communities.

Technology-Enabled Implementation and Monitoring

Modern technology has added a new dimension to urban housing delivery. Digital dashboards, geo-tagging and integrated monitoring systems have strengthened implementation under PMAY-U. These tools have improved transparency and enhanced project monitoring.

Unified Web Portal: The Unified Web Portal of PMAY-U 2.0 serves as a single digital platform for the implementation and monitoring of the scheme across urban areas. It enables eligible beneficiaries to apply for housing assistance and facilitates the processing and tracking of applications. The portal brings together key stakeholders, including beneficiaries, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), States/UTs and other implementing agencies, on one platform. It also facilitates geo-tagging of houses at different stages of construction and streamlines fund disbursement, ensuring transparency, accountability and efficient monitoring of the scheme.

PMAY-U Dashboard: The dashboard provides real-time progress on key performance indicators, accessible to States, UTs, ULBs/implementing agencies, Hon’ble MPs and MLAs, beneficiaries and all concerned stakeholders. This enables informed and data-driven decision-making and facilitates effective monitoring of implementation.

Geo-tagging: Projects are tracked across five stages starting from grounding, foundation, superstructure, finishing & external development, and completion. This staged monitoring ensures large-scale projects remain on schedule and meet quality benchmarks.

Technology Sub-Mission (TSM): This supports the adoption of modern, green and innovative construction technologies for faster and better-quality housing. Under TSM, Global Housing Technology Challenge – India (GHTC-India) was organized. A total of 54 proven technologies from across the world were shortlisted as mainstream, globally proven disaster-resilient technologies. Six Light House Projects (LHPs) using six distinct technologies shortlisted under GHTC-India are constructed at six places in the country.

Technology and Innovation Sub-Mission (TISM): Building on TSM’s progress, the Technology & Innovation Sub-Mission (TISM) under PMAY-U 2.0 promotes innovation in housing construction. It encourages innovative design, quality assurance, and adoption of green building standards for sustainable housing. TISM supports climate-responsive layouts and building plans across diverse geo-climatic zones.

Technology Innovation Grant (TIG): PMAY-U 2.0 provides an additional Technology Innovation Grant (TIG) for AHP projects. The grant supports the use of innovative and alternative technologies notified under the GHTC-India.

Impact on Beneficiary Lives

The real impact of PMAY-U is best understood through the lives it has transformed across urban India. These success stories reflect how secure housing has strengthened dignity, stability and self-reliance for beneficiaries.

A Roof of Their Own, A Future of Possibilities

Mandhalapu Ananthalakshmi lived with her husband and three children in a small house with a temporary roof in Addanki, Andhra Pradesh. The family depended on buffalo rearing for a modest income, and owning a permanent home seemed beyond their reach. After receiving support under PMAY-U, they overcame financial constraints by constructing the house themselves. The new pucca house brought safe sanitation, ended open defecation, and improved their quality of life. More importantly, it instilled confidence, inspiring the family to invest in their children’s future.

From Constant Repairs to Lasting Stability

In Nongpoh town, Meghalaya, Lucybon Syngkli supports her father and sisters as the family’s sole breadwinner. An ASHA worker and pineapple cultivator, she lived in a kutcha house that required frequent repairs, especially during the rainy season. The costs often strained the family’s finances and affected her father’s medical care. After becoming a PMAY-U beneficiary, Lucybon secured a permanent all-weather home, reducing maintenance expenses and improving the family’s financial stability. The savings help meet her father’s healthcare needs. The family has also adopted rainwater harvesting, planted fruit-bearing trees, received an LPG connection and switched to LED lighting. Their new home has brought peace of mind for the entire family.

Advancing the Vision of Housing for All

The story of a city is ultimately the story of the people who call it home. As urban centres grow and evolve, housing becomes one of the most visible indicators of inclusion, opportunity and quality of life. The journey of PMAY-U reflects this understanding. It has brought housing closer to millions who had long remained on the margins of urban development. In doing so, it has helped transform home ownership from an aspiration into a reality for countless households across the country. The Mission has also been strengthened by the use of technology-driven systems for planning, monitoring and transparent implementation. Through PMAY-U 2.0, the mission continues to ensure that every family has a safe place to call home.
