headline: PM Vishwakarma Completes Three Years: 30 Lakh Artisans Registered Under the Scheme
fullText:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises

PM Vishwakarma Completes Three Years: 30 Lakh Artisans Registered Under the Scheme

Third Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma to be Celebrated in Kolkata on 17th September 2026

Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari to Grace the Celebrations

16 SEP 2026 12:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, will celebrate the Third Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme on 17th September 2026 at the Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal. The event will mark three years of the implementation of the Scheme aimed at providing comprehensive and end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople and strengthening their livelihoods and entrepreneurial capabilities.

Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME, Government of India, along with Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister of West Bengal, will grace the occasion in the august presence of Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Minister of State for MSME, Government of India. Shri Dipak Barman, Minister-in-Charge, Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises & Textiles (MSME&T), Government of West Bengal, and Shri Ashok Dinda, Minister of State for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, will also grace the event.

Senior officials from the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, including representatives of the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC), and India Post, will also participate in the event.

The event will be attended by PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries, representatives of Gram Panchayats/Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Common Service Centres (CSCs)/Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs), and other stakeholders. An exhibition featuring various stalls showcasing products of local artisans and craftspeople will also be organised, providing them with a platform for the display and sale of their products.

Three Years of PM Vishwakarma

The PM Vishwakarma Scheme was launched by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 17th September 2023 with the objective of providing end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 identified trades. The Scheme seeks to strengthen the traditional skills of Vishwakarmas by providing them with institutional support, modern tools, access to finance, skill upgradation and market linkages, thereby enabling them to enhance their productivity, income and entrepreneurial potential.

The Scheme provides a comprehensive package of support comprising recognition through PM Vishwakarma certificates and identity cards, skill upgradation, toolkit incentive, credit support, incentives for digital transactions and marketing support.

In a significant milestone achieved within three years of its launch, 30 lakh beneficiaries have been registered under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme after completion of the prescribed three-stage verification process, thereby achieving the registration target under the Scheme. Around 24.50 lakh Vishwakarmas have also been provided Basic Skill Training by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

Under the credit component of the Scheme, 6.18 lakh Vishwakarmas have been provided loan support of up to ₹1 lakh at a concessional interest rate of 5% per annum, amounting to ₹5,297 crore. Further, 18.15 lakh modern toolkits have been delivered to Vishwakarmas at their doorsteps through India Post, helping artisans adopt improved tools and enhance the quality and productivity of their work.

PM Vishwakarma in West Bengal

The Government of West Bengal decided to onboard the Scheme in May 2026. Already, 3,000 beneficiaries have successfully registered after completing the three-stage verification process. Skill training is currently being imparted to the registered beneficiaries.

The Third Anniversary celebrations in Kolkata will also feature the distribution of PM Vishwakarma certificates, Basic Skill Training certificates, loan certificates and toolkits to beneficiaries. The event will provide an opportunity to recognise and celebrate the achievements of Vishwakarmas and highlight the impact of the Scheme at the grassroots level.

The celebrations will also showcase the traditional skills, products and entrepreneurial potential of artisans and craftspeople, providing them a platform to connect with wider markets and opportunities.

The Third Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma marks an important milestone in the Government’s continued efforts to preserve and promote traditional skills, equip artisans with modern tools and knowledge, facilitate access to institutional credit and markets, and enable Vishwakarmas to build sustainable livelihoods and emerge as successful entrepreneurs.

headline: National Webinar on Solid and e-Waste Management organised by the Department of School Education & Literacy
fullText:
Ministry of Education

National Webinar on Solid and e-Waste Management organised by the Department of School Education & Literacy

Quiz on Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 to be held for school students from September 17 to October 17, 2026

Target of 7 lakh cleanliness campaigns set under Special Campaign 6.0.

16 SEP 2026 9:06PM by PIB Delhi

A National Webinar on Solid and e-Waste Management was organised today in New Delhi, by the Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, as a lead-up to Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and Special Campaign 6.0.

Secretary, DoSEL, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar, highlighted the vision of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 towards inculcating environmental awareness and responsible citizenship among school students. He informed that under Special Campaign 5.0, around one lakh school students collected over 4,000 kgs of e-waste, across 10 cities in four States and one Union Territory. He added that effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 was essential for reducing pollution, conserving resources, promoting recycling and resource recovery and ensuring the safe and scientific management of waste.

Joint Secretary, DoSEL, Dr. Amarpreet Duggal, highlighted the pivotal role of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE in providing a valuable platform for students to understand environmental challenges and develop environmentally responsible attitudes, values and behaviour. She said that the convergence of Swachhata Pakhwada (September 1 to 15, 2026), Swachhata Hi Seva (September 17 - October 17, 2026) and Special Campaign 6.0 (October 2 to 31, 2026), should be seen as an opportunity to deepen the culture of cleanliness and responsible environmental practices among school students and the wider school community.

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, she also announced a Quiz Competition on “Solid Waste Management Rules 2026” for students from Grades 6th to 12th. The quiz will be hosted on the Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE portal from September 17 to October 17, 2026:

https://ecoclubs.education.gov.in/swachhata-hi-seva?start=quiz

The Webinar featured expert presentations on ‘Solid Waste Management’ and a walkthrough of the portal of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, providing participants with an overview of the digital platform and its resources for environmental awareness and student engagement.

Held under the aegis of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, the Webinar was aimed at sensitising school students and stakeholders on responsible waste management practices, source segregation, recycling, reuse and safe disposal of solid and electronic waste. More than 2.6 lakh school students, teachers and community members on YouTube participated in the Webinar.

A Portal for Special Campaign 6.0 was also launched today in another event. Speaking on the occasion, Secretary, DoSEL, informed that the Department had set a target of undertaking 7 lakh cleanliness campaigns across the country under Special Campaign 6.0.

Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Extends MoU with The Art of Living under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan

MoU Signed in New Delhi in the Presence of Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar

Renewed Partnership to Strengthen Awareness, Prevention and Community Mobilisation against Substance Abuse

16 SEP 2026 8:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, today extended its Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Non Profit, Spiritual, Educational & Humanitarian Organization ‘The Art of Living’, under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA). The MoU was signed at the Ministry’s Office in National Capital here.

The signing ceremony was held in the presence of Union Minister of Social Justice And Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Joint Secretary Dr. Sandeep R. Rathod, senior officers of the Ministry and representatives of ‘The Art of Living’.

Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Director (Drug Prevention), signed the MoU on behalf of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment while Shri Pankaj Narula, Trustee and authorised signatory, signed the MoU on behalf of ‘The Art of Living’.

Smt. Shabnam Awasthi, State Apex Member and Shri Vinay Sharma, Volunteer, ‘The Art of Living’, attended the ceremony as witnesses.

Through the renewed collaboration, the Department and ‘The Art of Living’ will continue to advance the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat by promoting a whole-of-society and whole- of –government approach to the prevention of substance abuse.

The renewed partnership is part of the Department’s continuing efforts under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to engage spiritual and value-based organizations in strengthening awareness, prevention and community mobilization against substance abuse.

Spiritual organizations, through their extensive community networks and grassroots presence, play an important role in promoting value-based living, strengthening individual and family resilience, reducing the stigma associated with substance use disorders, and encouraging affected persons to seek timely support and rehabilitation.

Pertinently, the Ministry has entered into MoUs with 12 spiritual organizations, including ‘The Art of Living’, Brahma Kumaris, Sant Nirankari Mission, ISKCON, Shri Ram Chandra Mission, All World Gayatri Pariwar, Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Dhanwantari Ashram, University of Patanjali, Divya Jyoti Jagrati Sansthan, Hare Krishna Movement, Adhyatm Vigyan Satsang Kendra and Chinmaya Mission.

India to Return as Official Partner Country at Gulfood 2027 for Second Consecutive Year

Gulfood 2027 to Widen Participation of MSMEs, FPOs, Startups and Women- and SC/ST-led Exporters

fullText:
Ministry of Law and Justice

Legislative Department Gears Up for Special Campaign 6.0 to Boost Cleanliness and Reduce Pendency

LEGISLATIVE DEPARTMENT, MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE FULLY COMMITTED TO PARTICIPATE IN SPECIAL CAMPAIGN 6

16 SEP 2026 8:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, is fully geared up to participate in the upcoming nationwide Special Campaign 6.0. This dedicated government initiative focuses on elevating cleanliness standards and significantly reducing workplace pendency across all ministries. The Government of India has scheduled the official execution of Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October to 31st October 2026. The Legislative Department is organising the Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, which will be executed in two phases.

Phase 1: Preparatory Phase (15th to 30th September 2026)

During this planning window, the department will lay the groundwork by identifying target areas and streamlining operational backlogs:

Space & Waste Assessment: Identifying specific cleanliness sites, upgrading space management, and scheduling the disposal of scrap, obsolete office items, and accumulated e-waste.

Clearing Pending References: Fast-tracking the disposal of high-priority communications, including references from Members of Parliament (MPs), State Governments, Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), and pending Parliamentary Assurances.

Grievance Redressal: Reviewing and resolving long-standing public grievances and official appeals.

Process Optimization: Improving record management systems and simplifying administrative rules and procedures for better governance.

Capacity Building: Organizing targeted training sessions, workshops, and awareness drives to align officers, staff, and support personnel with the campaign's goals.

Phase 2: Implementation Phase (2nd to 31st October 2026)

This phase will mark the active, on-ground execution of all planned activities:

Deep Cleaning Drives: Carrying out intensive, comprehensive cleaning of office premises, common corridors, washrooms, and surrounding facility areas.

Eco-Friendly Waste Disposal: Efficiently processing and disposing of all categorized e-waste and office scrap in an environmentally responsible manner.

Progress Monitoring: Establishing continuous daily monitoring and reporting mechanisms to maintain strict hygiene standards and ensure the campaign's ultimate success.

The Legislative Department reaffirms its commitment to building a clean, healthy, and sustainable working ecosystem. It calls upon all its officers and personnel to take active individual and collective responsibility to make this national drive a success.

Samrat/Pranab/ Sagar

The meeting underscored Government’s commitment to promote circular economy practices, supporting domestic steel manufacturing, and ensuring that India’s ship recycling industry continues to set global benchmarks in sustainability and efficiency.

Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to Organise ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ Ceremony on Seva Diwas

Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar to Light ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ Along with 200–250 Recovered Drug Users

Initiative to Highlight the Transformative Impact of Treatment and Rehabilitation in Overcoming Substance Use

16 SEP 2026 7:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will organise an ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ ceremony tomorrow evening at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre, in the National Capital here.

The programme is being held as part of the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’, being launched by the Government of India on the occasion of Seva Diwas.

Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr Virendra Kumar, will lead the ceremony and light the ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ along with 200–250 recovered drug users who have successfully undergone treatment and rehabilitation.

The participating beneficiaries have received support through Grant-in-Aid institutions of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and Addiction Treatment Facilities functioning under the De-addiction Programme in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas. Their participation will represent resilience, hope and the transformative impact of institutional support in helping individuals overcome substance use.

Joint Secretary Drug Prevention at the Ministry Dr Sandeep R Rathod said the programme will highlight the Ministry’s continued commitment to drug demand reduction and the treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration of affected persons into mainstream society. He said through the participation of recovered drug users, the Ministry seeks to inspire communities, demonstrate the positive outcomes of rehabilitation programmes and reinforce the message that recovery is possible through sustained care and collective support.

Dr Rathod stated that ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ initiative has been conceived to promote the values of service, respect and gratitude while recognizing beneficiaries of the Government’s flagship initiatives.

He said the lighting of the diya will symbolise empowerment, resilience and dignity, reaffirming the Ministry’s resolve to contribute to a healthier and more inclusive nation adding that the initiative also reflects the Government’s broader vision of service-oriented governance and the spirit of Seva Diwas.

Joint Secretary informed that under NAPDDR, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territories, NGOs and Government hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation.

Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan App

Dr Rathod stated that the Campaign has reached more than 34.55 crore citizens including over 13.71 Crore youth and 10.65 Crore women, through nationwide awareness activities. More than 1.68 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras (NMM) have also joined the campaign to strengthen community participation. In addition, over 31.40 lakh awareness and outreach activities were conducted across the country, he said.

The NMBA Portal is https://www.dosje.gov.in/organisation/nasha-mukt-bharat-abhiyaan/

Dr Rathod stated that the total Nasha Mukti Pledges including e-pledges taken account for more than 3.42 Lakh across the country as on date.

NMBA Pledge is an initiative to volunteer for reaching out to the victims of substance abuse. The pledge aims to encourage responsible behaviour to instil a sense of responsibility among people to stay away from drugs, to promote and foster sense of Unity and Commitment for encouraging stakeholders to work together towards a common goal. The Pledge further seeks to empower youth to contribute actively to developing a drug-free society.

The link of the NMBA e-Pledge is: https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/epledge

Dr Rathod further informed that more than 1.67 lakh master volunteers, community leaders and personnel have been trained in specialised addiction identification and caregiving workflows. These efforts strengthen community capacity to identify substance dependency and support individuals requiring care, he added.

He said to expand access to treatment, more than 755 new de-addiction facilities have been established in the last two years, that include District De-addiction Centres (DDACs), Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) and de-addiction centres in jails.

headline: PM chairs Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

PM chairs Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs

PM urges CEOs to actively participate in the next phase of India’s semiconductor growth

PM says India should aspire to be among the early leaders in emerging technologies

PM reiterates Government’s commitment to a predictable and responsive policy environment

PM invites industry leaders to share suggestions on policy and administrative measures

CEOs appreciate PM’s leadership and Government’s sustained efforts to strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem

CEOs express confidence in India’s potential to build capabilities across the semiconductor value chain

16 SEP 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs at Seva Teerth earlier today.

During the meeting, Prime Minister emphasised the importance of close collaboration between the Government and the semiconductor industry in shaping India’s technology future. He highlighted India’s strong foundation of talent, technology adoption and infrastructure, and called for greater industry participation in skilling, innovation and emerging technologies such as AI and Quantum Computing. Referring to the target of training one crore people in AI, he said India’s talent pool, combined with the experience and capabilities of global industry leaders, can create significant opportunities.

Prime Minister said India should aspire to be among the early leaders in emerging technologies. He noted the significant progress made in the semiconductor sector and said the ecosystem is now moving from foundational efforts to a phase of greater scale and opportunity.

Prime Minister reiterated the Government’s commitment to a predictable and responsive policy environment, while emphasising that policies must evolve in line with technological advancements and industry requirements. The World Circular Economy Forum 2026 (WCEF2026) concluded today at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, after two days of intense discussions spanning the full spectrum of Circular Economy. The programme also featured the WCEF2026 highlight film and launch of the Ecomark logo.

He stated that the true impact of the event lies in the collaborations on the ground for Circular Solutions and stressed on the need to move forward together from commitment to action. The Minister highlighted that the circular economy is not merely an environmental agenda but an economic opportunity, a societal responsibility, a daily lifestyle, and a pathway to secure a sustainable future for generations to come.

headline: Care That Goes Beyond the Prescription
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Care That Goes Beyond the Prescription

Affordable healthcare products for every stage of life

16 SEP 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

It takes a village to raise a child, goes the adage. But it does not say who bears the cost. A small family, familiar with its routine and planned expenses, welcomes a new life. Suddenly, everything finds a new rhythm. There are late nights, baby diapers and wipes, doctor visits, medicines, and countless little decisions that come with loving and caring for a newborn. The joy is immense. So are the responsibilities and expenses.

From baby care to post-partum care, healthcare products have become an indispensable part of family life when the nest grows. Medicines form an important part of this expenditure, but they are far from the only expense. The need for healthcare products continues when someone is recovering after surgery or when families are caring for aged parents and dependents.

It is in this larger context of affordable healthcare beyond medicines that the Government is steadily expanding the reach of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP). With a network of over 20,000 Janaushadhi Kendras across the country, the initiative offers an expansive range of affordable surgical and healthcare products. This brings them closer to families and their everyday needs. Together, these products form a healthcare basket designed to meet changing needs across every stage of life.

PMBJP: Taking Affordable Medicines Closer to People

Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana provides quality-assured generic medicines at significantly lower prices. This is enabled through an expanding network of dedicated Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) across the country. The initiative strengthens the affordability and access to generic pharmaceuticals.

The product basket under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojna has 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals, medical consumables and devices, as of August 2026. This covers all major therapeutic groups, such as cardiovascular, anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, anti-infectives, anti-allergic and gastro-intestinal medicines and nutraceuticals.

During the last five financial years i.e. 2021-22 to 2025-26, PMBJP has made sales of ₹7,873.85 crore through Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country. This has led to savings of approximately ₹37,200 crore to the citizens.

For a young family, the arrival of a child marks the beginning of a new set of everyday needs. Through Janaushadhi Bachpan, families can access essential infant-care products at affordable prices through Janaushadhi Kendras. The basket includes baby diapers in different sizes and wipes. Baby Wipes, available in a pack of 20 at ₹45, offer an affordable option for one of the most frequently used baby-care essentials. The basket also includes Baby Feeding Bottles (250 ml), Manual Breast Pumps, Hot Water Bags and Infant Feeding Tubes, etc.

But the journey of care also includes the mother. Recovery after childbirth requires adequate rest, support, and attention to physical well-being. Abdominal Belts are available through the Janaushadhi network to support post-delivery care. Cervical Pillows, priced at ₹525, offer comfort and support and can be useful during pregnancy and beyond.

As the child grows, the needs change too. A growing child may sometimes require supportive equipment at home for respiratory issues and other health conditions. Access to affordable healthcare devices can therefore become particularly important for families.

Janaushadhi Kendras offer Electrical Nebulizer Machines at ₹937.50 and Nebulizer Masks with Tubing for children at ₹200. The Janaushadhi basket is increasingly offering products that support not only treatment, but also monitoring, recovery, and day-to-day healthcare management.

Regular health monitoring can itself become part of everyday life. Glucometer Test Strips (25 strips), priced at ₹500, are available through the Janaushadhi network for regular blood sugar monitoring. Pulse Oximeters, used to measure blood oxygen saturation, are also part of the available range of medical devices.

And as parents and other family members grow older, the responsibility of care often becomes an integral part of family life. For aged, dependent, or bedridden individuals, healthcare extends beyond treatment. Hygiene, comfort, dignity and everyday caregiving become equally important.

For families caring for a loved one over an extended period, such products can become recurring purchases. Even modest savings on frequently used healthcare products can therefore translate into meaningful financial relief over months and years.

Recognising this need, the Government has introduced Jan Aushadhi Swabhiman, a dedicated range of adult diapers. From the first days of parenthood to childhood, from regular health monitoring to caring for ageing loved ones, a family's healthcare journey is continuous. So are the expenses that accompany it. The Janaushadhi basket of surgicals and consumables aims to address these needs.

It is also set to expand further, with several healthcare and supportive-care products currently in process and in the pipeline for inclusion through the network. These include Range of Motion-Knee Brace, Walker (Sit Assist-to-Stand Support), Medical Steam Vaporizer, Foot Elevator Pillow, Pregnancy Back Support Belt and Cervical Collar.

The proposed expansion reflects the Government's continued efforts to broaden affordable healthcare beyond medicines and make a wider range of essential healthcare, mobility, rehabilitation and supportive-care products accessible to all citizens.

headline: CSIR Transfers Technologies for Sustainable Leather Processing and Safer, Greener Roads to Industry
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

CSIR Transfers Technologies for Sustainable Leather Processing and Safer, Greener Roads to Industry

16 SEP 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) organised a Technology Transfer Event at CSIR Headquarters, New Delhi, today, bringing together technologies developed by CSIR-Central Leather Research Institute (CSIR-CLRI), Chennai, and CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), New Delhi, for transfer to industry.

The event, held at the SSB Auditorium, CSIR Headquarters, included presentations of the technologies by the two laboratories, followed by their transfer to industry. Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, CSIR, addressed the gathering. The programme also included remarks by the Directors of CSIR-CLRI and CSIR-CRRI.

The technologies showcased for transfer reflect CSIR’s continuing emphasis on taking laboratory-developed solutions towards industrial deployment and addressing challenges relating to sustainability, circular economy, waste utilisation, road safety and infrastructure.

CSIR-CLRI technologies turn industrial waste into valuable resources

CSIR-CLRI presented a technology for producing protein-based syntans from chrome shavings, addressing an important waste-management challenge of the leather industry. Chrome shavings are a non-biodegradable solid waste, but they contain valuable collagen protein that often remains underutilised. The CSIR-CLRI process recovers chromium-free protein hydrolysate from this waste and converts it into acrylic-, phenolic- and melamine-based syntans that can be reused in leather retanning.

The technology has been demonstrated at the 100–200 kg pilot scale and validated at a commercial scale of 1,500 kg. According to CSIR-CLRI, its adoption can lead to up to 50 per cent reduction in total dissolved solids (TDS) in the post-tanning stream. The patented technology has been industry-validated and is ready for commercial licensing.

Another CSIR-CLRI technology focuses on the sustainable valorisation of spent pickling acid, a highly acidic waste stream generated during steel processing. The process enables recovery of iron and chloride from spent pickling acid and their conversion into value-added products, including pigment-grade iron oxide and ammonium chloride.

The technology seeks to convert a hazardous industrial waste into commercially useful products while reducing environmental pollution and strengthening domestic manufacturing. It is aligned with circular-economy principles and contributes to Sustainable Development Goals relating to clean water and sanitation, industry and innovation, and responsible consumption and production.

CSIR-CRRI technologies address road safety and pothole repair

CSIR-CRRI presented two technologies for transfer to industry: ClariVisor – A Glare Mitigation Device for Four-Wheelers and a Two Pack Onsite Pothole Filling Mix.

ClariVisor is designed as an in-vehicle glare mitigation solution for four-wheelers. The technology has been designed for fitment within the same footprint as the vehicle’s original equipment manufacturer (OEM) sun visor, without requiring structural changes to the vehicle.

The Two Pack Onsite Pothole Filling Mix offers a cold-application approach to road repair. The material is supplied in two separate packs for on-site blending and immediate application. Unlike conventional hot-mix approaches, it does not require a hot-mix plant or heating, thereby reducing energy consumption and emissions. The technology is solvent-free and enables faster repair and early reopening of roads to traffic.

The technologies being transferred build on CSIR-CRRI’s wider portfolio of innovations in sustainable and resilient road infrastructure.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi emphasised the importance of accelerating the translation of CSIR technologies from laboratories to industry and ensuring that scientific research delivers tangible societal, environmental and economic impact. The DG, CSIR highlighted that stronger partnerships between CSIR laboratories and industry are essential for scaling indigenous technologies and enhancing their reach and impact.

The Technology Transfer Event underscores CSIR’s focus on strengthening industry partnerships and moving proven indigenous technologies towards wider commercial deployment. Through such technology transfers, CSIR continues to advance its mandate of translating science and technology into solutions that contribute to sustainable industrial development, improved infrastructure and national economic growth.

headline: CAQM conducts special inspection of industries in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh; 16 of 22 units inspected found non-compliant, 12 Show Cause Notices issued
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

CAQM conducts special inspection of industries in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh; 16 of 22 units inspected found non-compliant, 12 Show Cause Notices issued

16 SEP 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) conducted a special inspection of industries operating in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh, on 15.09.2026, during which 22 industrial units were inspected, 16 were found non-compliant with applicable norms and Statutory Directions and 12 Show Cause Notices (SCNs) were issued.

The inspection drive was carried out by 7 Flying Squads of CAQM in coordination with the District Administration and concerned authorities. The inspections covered industrial areas of Masuri-Gulawati Road, Pilkhuwa, Ravali/Shekhpur/M.G. Road, Tatarpur/Garh Road, Railway Road/Textile Centre Road and Ravala/Shekhar. Of the 22 units inspected, 6 were found compliant, while 16 were found non-compliant with the applicable norms and Statutory Directions.

Various instances of non-compliance were observed during the inspections, including intense visible smoke, inadequate Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs), non-installation or improper functioning of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS), bypass arrangements in wet scrubber systems and leakages in APCD/wet scrubber systems. Non-compliance of DG sets with statutory

directions, discrepancies in Consent to Operate (CTO) and DG set capacity/fuel details, non-availability of stack emission reports and stacks not conforming to Emission Regulation Part-III (ERP-III) guidelines were also observed.

During the inspection drive, entry was denied by two suspected illegal units. Accordingly, strict action/re-inspections have been proposed. Instances of illegal/non-conforming industrial units, use of a wood-fired pit furnace with hazardous sludge, and non-installation of stack monitoring/Retrofitted Emission Control Device (RECD) systems were also observed. One unit using a wood-fired pit furnace with hazardous sludge and another non-conforming unit were sealed by the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB).

The inspection teams also identified industrial units operating in compliance with the applicable norms. The findings of the inspection teams have been documented for further necessary action by the concerned authorities.

Based on the observations made during the inspection drive, 12 Show Cause Notices (SCNs) have been issued to the concerned units. CAQM has reiterated that all industrial units are required to strictly comply with applicable environmental norms, Statutory Directions, CTO conditions and other prescribed measures. Any instance of non-compliance shall be dealt with in accordance with applicable environmental laws and regulations. The concerned authorities have been advised to take necessary action(s) to ensure compliance.

CAQM continues to undertake special inspection drives across NCR to identify instances of non-compliance, strengthen enforcement and ensure effective implementation of Statutory Directions by industries and other pollution-generating sectors.

Empowering CPSEs for Global and Domestic Debt Markets: DPE Holds Interactive Workshop with Leading Credit Rating Agencies

Secretary, DPE underlines the role of objective credit ratings in benchmarking public sector creditworthiness and securing cost-effective funding

16 SEP 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the Standing Conference of Public Enterprises (SCOPE), as part of its ongoing capacity-building initiatives on CPSE management, organized a half-day interactive workshop today for Maharatna and Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) with select International and Domestic Credit Rating agencies, in New Delhi.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri K. Moses Chalai, Secretary, DPE, highlighted the robust operational performance of CPSEs and their pivotal contribution to India's economic growth also highlighted both the opportunities and challenges being faced by the CPSEs. He emphasized the need to make credit rating processes more transparent, efficient, and aligned with the realities of the Indian context.

Setting the context, Dr. Vasundhara Upmanyu, Joint Secretary, DPE, noted that rating agencies provide an objective, independent assessment of financial strength, risk, and credibility, underscoring the necessity for sustained dialogue between CPSEs and credit assessors. Earlier, Dr. Atul Sobti, Director General, SCOPE, welcomed the dignitaries and delegates in his opening remarks.

Technical presentations on rating methodologies, risk pricing, and debt-market dynamics were delivered by CareEdge Global IFSC Limited, CARE Ratings Limited, CRISIL Ratings Limited, ICRA Ratings Limited, and Infomerics Valuation and Rating Limited.

headline: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Launches Web Portal for Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0; Calls Swachhata a Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Nation Movement
fullText:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Launches Web Portal for Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0; Calls Swachhata a Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Nation Movement

Swachhata campaign launched in 2021 has evolved from a simple cleanliness initiative into a whole-of-government and whole-of-nation movement, and has so far earned Rs 5,000 crores through scrap disposal: Dr Jitendra Singh

Special Campaign 6 to Strengthen Scientific Waste Management, E-Waste Disposal and Reduction of Pendency: Dr Jitendra Singh

Swachhata Campaign Freed 1,000 Lakh Sq. Ft. Office Space, Cleared Around 2 Crore Files and Generated ₹5,000 Crore from Scrap Disposal Over Five Years: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Swachhata Campaign Has Become a People’s Movement Driving Behavioural Change and Better Governance, Says Dr Jitendra Singh

16 SEP 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today launched the Web Portal for Special Campaign 6, saying that the Swachhata campaign launched in 2014 has evolved from a simple cleanliness initiative into a whole-of-government and whole-of-nation movement, and has so far earned Rs 5,000 crores has been earned through scrap disposal, bringing about behavioural change, improving efficiency in government functioning and creating economic value from waste.

Addressing the launch programme Dr. Jitendra Singh said the campaign reflects the citizen-centric approach of the Government and demonstrates how a national call can become a people’s movement when it addresses foundational issues affecting the everyday lives of citizens.

The launch event was attended by Secretary, Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma; Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy, Shri T.K. Anil Kumar; Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra; Secretary, Department of Posts, Shri Subrat Das; senior officers and nodal officers representing various Ministries and Departments, besides media representatives.

The campaign has demonstrated that systematic cleanliness and waste management can also generate substantial economic value. Over the last five years, 5,000 crores have been earned through scrap disposal, while 1,000 lakh square feet of office space has been freed, more than 24 lakh cleanliness campaign sites have been undertaken and around 2 crore files have been weeded out for improved record management. These achievements reflect the expansion of the campaign beyond cleanliness to efficient utilisation of government resources, reduction of pendency, better use of public spaces and conversion of waste into wealth.

Recalling the beginning of the Swachhata initiative, Dr. Jitendra Singh said cleanliness was among the earliest priorities of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi after the Government assumed office in 2014. The Prime Minister’s emphasis on Swachhata in his first Independence Day address on August 15, 2014, brought a foundational issue affecting the everyday lives of common citizens to the centre of the governance agenda. The initiative, he said, also set the tone for a departure from the conventional status quo approach and greater emphasis on citizen-centric governance.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the response to the Swachhata campaign demonstrated how a clear national call can lead to widespread public participation and behavioural change. Recalling the emphasis on construction of toilets, particularly for women, he spoke about the hardships faced by women in rural and suburban areas and the difficulties experienced by school-going girls because of inadequate sanitation facilities. He cited an instance from his own constituency where a Class 9 girl had stopped attending school until a toilet was constructed at her home and school. A subsequent survey found around 200 households facing similar concerns, bringing to light a significant issue that had remained largely unaddressed.

The Minister said one of the major outcomes of the sustained Swachhata campaign has been a change in public behaviour, with people becoming increasingly conscious about littering and cleanliness in public spaces. At the same time, the campaign has changed the perception of waste by demonstrating its economic value through the principle of “Waste to Wealth”.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Special Campaign has become one of the early examples of a “whole-of-government plus whole-of-nation” effort. The initiative initially began with cleaning of files and offices and subsequently expanded to freeing up spaces, improving utilisation of public areas and systematic disposal of scrap. Recalling the early experience, he said around 20 crore was initially generated through scrap disposal, demonstrating the economic value of discarded government material and the potential of systematic disposal to generate resources.

The Minister also spoke about the campaign’s contribution to improving workplace discipline and timely clearance of files. He said dashboards and online feedback mechanisms have enabled Ministries and Departments to assess their progress from time to time and improve implementation. Recalling instances of neglected and inaccessible spaces in government establishments, he said the campaign also provided an opportunity to identify such areas, clear them and put them to productive use.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the dedicated campaign period from October 2, Gandhi Jayanti, to October 31, Sardar Patel Jayanti, should not be seen as a period during which cleanliness activities are undertaken only for a month. Rather, the campaign serves as an annual reiteration of the resolve and commitment to maintain cleanliness, efficiency and responsiveness throughout the year. He said the experience accumulated through successive editions has provided a strong foundation for Special Campaign 6 and would enable the campaign to move forward with greater focus and effectiveness.

Secretary, DARPG, Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, said Special Campaign 6 is not merely about cleaning files and offices but about redefining the culture of governance by making efficiency, cleanliness and responsiveness an everyday feature of government functioning. She said the campaign has grown into a nationwide movement involving offices and public spaces across the country, including remote locations, public sector undertakings, autonomous organisations, missions abroad and citizen-facing establishments such as post offices, schools and railway stations.

She said Special Campaign 6 would build on the experience of scientific waste management with particular emphasis on effective collection, segregation and environmentally sound disposal of e-waste in compliance with the e-waste management rules. The upgraded digital platform will enable real-time monitoring during the preparatory, implementation and evaluation phases and will include a dedicated module for tracking e-waste. She called upon Ministries and Departments to participate with renewed energy and collectively achieve better results than the previous year.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Special Campaign should be seen not merely as an annual cleanliness exercise but as a continuing commitment to better governance. He said the campaign has created greater awareness among citizens, brought discipline into government functioning, unlocked the value of waste and contributed to improving the esteem of government institutions as well as society as a whole. As Special Campaign 6 moves forward, he said, the accumulated experience of the past editions provides an opportunity to carry the campaign forward with greater participation, efficiency and sustained commitment.

headline: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Begins Preparations for Special Campaign 6.0
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Begins Preparations for Special Campaign 6.0

Special Campaign 6.0 to Focus on Cleanliness and Timely Disposal of Pending Matters

Campaign to be implemented from 2nd to 31st October, 2026 across Secretariat and field offices in line with DARPG guidelines

16 SEP 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, has initiated preparations for Special Campaign 6.0, which will be implemented across the Department from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, in line with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The Campaign will focus on institutionalizing cleanliness practices, improving space management and ensuring timely disposal of pending matters in Government offices.

Building on the achievements of the previous Special Campaign, DDWS has continued its efforts towards reducing pendency and ensuring timely disposal of various categories of references and public matters. The progress has been regularly monitored and updated on the SCDPM Portal of DARPG.

During the period from 1st November 2025 to 31st August 2026, notable achievements include:

67 References from Members of Parliament were disposed of.

21 Parliamentary Assurances were resolved.

03 IMC References (Cabinet Proposals) were disposed of.

13 State Government References were resolved.

11 PMO References were disposed of.

10378 Public Grievances were disposed of.

2346 Public Grievance Appeals were resolved.

This year Campaign will accord special emphasis to scientific management of e-waste, with focus on effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste in accordance with the applicable rules and procedures. This will contribute towards environmentally responsible office management and sustainable workplace practices.

With Special Campaign 6.0, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation reaffirms its commitment in making cleanliness an integral part of daily office practices and ensuring the timely resolution of public matters in the spirit of transparency, efficiency and citizen-centric governance.
